Instructions For LLM:
Lower values imply more attractive (cheaper) valuation

- If user requests **“undervalued”, “cheap”,** or **“value”**, pick the lowest threshold available (e.g., **“Under 5”** or **“Under 10”**).

P/B Ratio
Shows how much investors pay for each dollar of book value (assets – liabilities); lower values often highlight balance-sheet bargains.
• If user requests ‘undervalued’, ‘cheap’, or ‘value’, set the filter to Under 1.
• If user requests ‘fair value’, apply > 2 and < 3 in the same filter.
• If user requests ‘high-valuation’ or ‘over-valued’, set the filter to > 10.

P/S Ratio
Indicates how much the market pays for each dollar of revenue; low readings can flag inexpensive sales multiples.
• If user requests ‘undervalued’, ‘cheap’, or ‘value’, set the filter to Under 1.
• If user requests ‘fair value’, apply > 2 and < 4 in the same filter.
• If user requests ‘high-valuation’ or ‘over-valued’, set the filter to > 10.

P/E Ratio
Measures price relative to earnings; a classic valuation gauge where lower numbers suggest a cheaper profit multiple.
• If user requests ‘undervalued’, ‘cheap’, or ‘value’, set the filter to Under 10.
• If user requests ‘fair value’, apply > 15 and < 20 in the same filter.
• If user requests ‘high-valuation’ or ‘over-valued’, set the filter to > 20.

EV/EBITDA
Compares enterprise value to operating cash earnings; useful across different capital structures—lower may signal bargain pricing.
• If user requests ‘undervalued’, ‘cheap’, or ‘value’, set the filter to Under 5.
• If user requests ‘fair value’, apply > 8 and < 12 in the same filter.
• If user requests ‘high-valuation’ or ‘over-valued’, set the filter to > 20.

EV/Sales Ratio
Expresses a company’s total valuation (enterprise value) relative to its annual revenue; lower multiples mean investors are paying less for each dollar of sales.
• If user requests ‘undervalued’, ‘cheap’, or ‘value’, set the filter to Under 2 (captures the lowest threshold available).
• If user requests ‘fair value’ (or gives no valuation preference), apply > 3 and < 6 together in the same filter (targets a moderate, mid-range multiple).
• If user requests ‘high-valuation’ or ‘over-valued’, set the filter to > 20 (identifies stocks trading at very rich sales multiples).

Net Profit Margin
Percentage of revenue that ultimately becomes net income—captures overall profitability after all costs and taxes.
• If the user asks for “high margin,” “very profitable,” or “efficient operators,” choose High > 25%.
• If the user wants “solid” or “average” profitability (or gives no preference), choose Moderate 11–25%.
• If the user mentions “thin margins” or “low profitability,” choose Low 0–10%.
• For “unprofitable” or “loss-making” firms, choose Negative < 0%.

Operating Profit Margin
Operating income as a share of revenue—shows core operating efficiency before interest and taxes.
• High > 20% for “strong operations” or “wide operating margin.”
• Moderate 11–20% for “average” or unspecified.
• Low 0–10% for “low margin.”
• Negative < 0% for “operating losses.”

EBIT Margin
EBIT divided by revenue—similar to operating margin but after depreciation & amortization.
• High > 20% when user requests “robust EBIT margin.”
• Moderate 11–20% for neutral requests.
• Low 0–10% for “low EBIT.”
• Negative < 0% for loss situations.

Gross Profit Margin
Revenue minus cost of goods sold, as a percentage of revenue—measures product-level pricing power.
• High > 60% for “high gross margin” or “premium pricing.”
• Moderate 30–59% for “steady” or no preference.
• Low 0–29% for “commodity-like,” “low margin.”
• Negative < 0% for firms selling below cost.

Return on Assets (ROA)
Net income relative to total assets—gauges how effectively the company turns assets into profit.
• High > 25% for “asset-light, very efficient.”
• Moderate 11–25% for “healthy” or no preference.
• Low 0–10% for “low ROA.”
• Negative < 0% for “asset-destroying” or loss-making.

EBITDA Margin
EBITDA divided by revenue—shows cash-operating profitability, independent of capital structure.
• High > 30% for “strong cash margins.”
• Moderate 16–30% for neutral requests.
• Low 0–15% for “low cash margin.”
• Negative < 0% for negative EBITDA.

Return on Equity (ROE)
Net income relative to shareholders’ equity—high values indicate attractive returns for owners.
• High > 25% for “high ROE” or “shareholder-efficient.”
• Moderate 11–25% for average.
• Low 0–10% for “low ROE.”
• Negative < 0% for negative equity returns.
